name: SN74LVC2T45DCUR
title: SN74LVC2T45: 2-bit dual-supply bus transceiver, 1.65 V to 5.5 V on each port, DIR-controlled
summary: A two-channel noninverting level translator with separate supplies for its A side (VCCA) and B side (VCCB), each set anywhere from 1.65 V to 5.5 V. One DIR input, powered from VCCA, picks the direction for both channels: high for A to B, low for B to A. Outputs are push-pull, ±24 mA at 3.3 V, and data rates reach 420 Mbps from 3.3 V to 5 V. Ioff and VCC isolation put every I/O in high impedance when the part, or either one of its supplies, is off. Packages: SM8 (DCT), VSSOP (DCU) and 8-ball DSBGA (YZP).
key_figures: VCCA and VCCB each 1.65 V to 5.5 V

circuits.title: Unidirectional logic level shifting
circuits.description: Two signals pass one way only, from SYSTEM-2 (supply VCC2) to SYSTEM-1 (supply VCC1). DIR is wired to ground, so the B port is the input side and the A port drives. Two SYSTEM-2 buffers powered from VCC2 drive B1 and B2; A1 and A2 feed two SYSTEM-1 buffers powered from VCC1. VCCA comes from VCC1 and VCCB from VCC2, each 1.65 V to 5.5 V.
notes: The design steps: the driving device's supply sets the input range, which must clear the input port's VIH for a high and stay under its VIL for a low; the driven device's supply sets the output range.

circuits.title: Bidirectional logic level shifting
circuits.description: One bidirectional line between SYSTEM-1 (VCC1) and SYSTEM-2 (VCC2) runs through the A2/B2 channel. A SYSTEM-1 output, DIR CTRL, sets the direction at DIR. Each side of the line has a pullup, pulldown or bus-hold that keeps it at a known level while both ports are off during a turnaround. The unused channel's A1 and B1 are tied to ground. Because the part has no output enable, the two systems must avoid driving the line at the same time while the direction changes.
notes: (1) Both sides use the same bias: both pullup or both pulldown.
The turnaround follows the data transmission sequence table; an output is valid after the enable time given by the enable-time equations.

circuits.title: Test load circuit
circuits.description: The output under test sees CL and RL to ground, plus a second RL to switch S1. S1 is open for propagation delays, at 2 × VCCO for tPLZ/tPZL and at GND for tPHZ/tPZH. CL is 15 pF and each RL 2 kΩ at every VCCO.

operation.text: Two noninverting transceiver channels between an A port powered by VCCA and a B port powered by VCCB. Each supply can be anywhere from 1.65 V to 5.5 V, independently, so the part moves logic between any pair of 1.8 V, 2.5 V, 3.3 V and 5 V systems. DIR high passes data from A to B; DIR low passes data from B to A. Both channels follow the one DIR pin, and DIR is powered from VCCA.
Maximum data rates: 420 Mbps translating 3.3 V to 5 V, 210 Mbps translating to 3.3 V, 140 Mbps translating to 2.5 V, 75 Mbps translating to 1.8 V.

The input stages of both ports stay on whichever way DIR points, so every data pin needs a valid high or low; a floating pin raises ICC and ICCZ. Unused I/Os are best tied to GND, and no I/O may float while the direction is being changed.
With the part unpowered, its inputs and outputs go high impedance and the Ioff circuitry blocks damaging backflow current into the part. Leakage at any pin in this state is the Ioff figure.
If either supply is at GND while the other is still applied, all I/Os on both ports go high impedance. Leakage is again bounded by Ioff.

Balanced push-pull CMOS outputs that source and sink about equally: ±24 mA at 3.3 V, up to 32 mA at 4.5 V to 5.5 V. Their edges are fast into light loads, so line impedance and loading need attention to avoid ringing. The outputs can deliver more current than the part survives, so the absolute maximum current and thermal limits apply. Two outputs may be paralleled for more drive.

Ground goes on first. After that the supplies may come up or down in any order and at any ramp rate without a glitch on the I/Os, so a downstream device does not see a false bit, reset or configuration.

Each VCC pin wants its own bypass capacitor as near the pin as possible: 0.1 µF suits a single-supply part; with several VCC pins, 0.01 µF or 0.022 µF on each. Capacitors may be paralleled for different noise frequencies; 0.1 µF with 1 µF is common.

Static supply current is at most 4 µA for ICCA + ICCB across 1.65 V to 5.5 V on both rails; typical totals are 2 µA or less at every supply pair. With both supplies at 3 V to 5.5 V, one input held at its rail minus 0.6 V raises the supply current by up to 50 µA (ΔICC).

There is no output-enable pin, so turning the bus around goes through DIR: the driving system stops, both ports are left high impedance with the lines held by matched pullups or pulldowns, DIR flips, and only then does the other side start driving. A new output is valid after the enable time.

Bypass both supplies, keep traces short to limit loading, and leave pads on the signal paths for load capacitors or pullup resistors so rise and fall times can be tuned. A layout example has a bypass capacitor beside VCCA (pin 1) and one beside VCCB (pin 8), each with a via to the power plane and a via to the inner ground plane. A1 and A2 come from the controller, B1 and B2 go to the system, and DIR (pin 5) is pulled to VCCA through a resistor, setting A to B.
